info.title: TwitterAPIs API
info.description: REST API for Twitter and X data. Search tweets and users, resolve a single tweet into its full thread, read profiles and timelines, page the follower graph, and run write actions over plain HTTP with Bearer auth and JSON. Pay per call: almost every call is $0.0008 (standard reads plus simple write actions like, retweet, bookmark, follow, their undos, and delete), tweet/thread is $0.004, full tweet history is $0.0024, tweet creation and DM reads are $0.0016, and account reads are free. New accounts start with $0.50 in free credits.

post.description: Files a product feedback report against your account. It exists for AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, any MCP client) working against this API: when a call fails, a capability is missing, or the user asks for it, the agent drafts a report locally, the user reviews it, and the client sends it here. The report reaches the team as a stored row plus a Slack post, and the returned id lets the agent read its status later. Free, never metered, rate limited to 10 per minute per key. Cost: Free per call.

201.description: File a bug, idea or missing-capability report from the tool you are using, typically drafted by your AI agent and sent after you review it.

id.description: The report's id (a UUID). Pass it to GET feedback/{id} to read its status and the team's response.

type.description: One of bug, idea or missing_capability. Anything else is rejected with 400 naming type.

title.description: One line, 1 to 120 characters after trimming. Say what broke or what is missing, not how the user feels about it.
title.example: tweet/thread returns 500 on a quoted reply

details.description: 1 to 8000 characters. Recommended shape, three labelled bullets: what happened (observed vs expected, the exact error text if short), repro (minimal steps), evidence (endpoint, status, request id, tool name, client, version), optionally after a one-line summary of the goal. No quotes of the conversation.
details.example: what happened: tweet/thread?id=1899999999999999999 answered 500 server_error, expected the 4-post thread. repro: GET tweet/thread with that id. evidence: status 500, request id req_01J9K2, twitter_tweet_thread via claude-code/2.1.259.

evidence.description: Identifiers only, never payloads: tool, endpoint, status, request_id, client, mcp_version. Must serialize to 4096 bytes or fewer, and must be a JSON object (an array is rejected); either failure is a 400 naming evidence.

client.description: The calling agent or tool and its version, so a fix can be matched to what sent the report. Up to 120 characters.

get.description: Returns the calling account's own feedback reports, newest first, keyset-paginated on (created_at desc, id desc). Each item carries the same summary fields as GET feedback/{id} (id, type, title, area, status, response, created_at, updated_at) and never details or evidence, so paging this endpoint can never turn into a bulk export of a report's full body: read one by id to get that. Free, never metered, and shares the 10-per-minute limiter with POST feedback and GET feedback/{id}. Cost: Free per call.

200.description: Read back the session you registered: which X account it resolved to, whether it is still alive, and whether the proxy you supplied is the one your writes leave from. Free.

registered.description: True when a session is stored for your API key. False when you never registered one, or revoked it. Per-call credentials sent as x-auth-token and x-ct0 are never stored, so a caller who only uses that path always sees false.

username.description: The X handle the stored session resolved to when it was registered. Read back from storage, not from anything you send, so it is the field that settles whether you are acting as the account you expect. Null when resolution never succeeded.

twitter_user_id.description: The numeric X user id for the same account. Null when resolution never succeeded.

status.description: Either ok or dead. dead is stamped when X rejects the cookies as expired or deauthorized, so it is an observation rather than a guess. A dead session is still stored and still revocable; re-register to resume.

created_at.description: ISO timestamp of when this session was first registered.

updated_at.description: ISO timestamp of the last time the session was registered or replaced. Equal to created_at when it has never been re-registered.

last_used_at.description: ISO timestamp of the last call that acted as this session. Null if it has never been used. A last_used_at that stopped moving is often the first sign of a stalled integration.

source.description: Which egress tier a write on this session would use: session (the proxy you registered), sticky_residential or pool_residential (an exit we assign and keep stable for this account), or direct (our shared server IP).

customer_proxy_in_use.description: True when the proxy_url you registered is the one your writes leave from. This is the direct answer to whether your own proxy is being honoured.

note.description: One line explaining that tier and what to do about it. On the direct tier it explains why a shared IP raises the chance of a challenge.

message.description: Human-readable summary. Differs for a live session, a dead one, and no session at all.

egress.note: Writes leave through the proxy you registered on this session. Keep it sticky, one dedicated IP per account, and geo-matched to where the account normally signs in.

post.description: Log in to an X account with a username and password (plus a TOTP secret when two-factor authentication is enabled). cURL: Paginate all pages
x-codeSamples.source:
# Walk every page until the collection array comes back empty.
cursor=""
while : ; do
  resp=$(curl -s "https://api.twitterapis.com/twitter/tweet/advanced_search?query=from:naval&cursor=$cursor" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TWITTERAPIS_KEY")
  count=$(echo "$resp" | jq '.tweets | length')
  [ "$count" -eq 0 ] && break
  echo "$resp" | jq '.tweets[]'
  cursor=$(echo "$resp" | jq -r '.next_cursor // ""')
  [ -z "$cursor" ] || [ "$cursor" = "null" ] && break
done

# Walk every page until the collection array comes back empty.
cursor=""
while : ; do
  resp=$(curl -s "https://api.twitterapis.com/twitter/tweet/quotes?id=1759123456789012345&cursor=$cursor" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TWITTERAPIS_KEY")
  count=$(echo "$resp" | jq '.tweets | length')

  cursor=$(echo "$resp" | jq -r '.next_cursor // ""')
  [ -z "$cursor" ] || [ "$cursor" = "null" ] && break

cursor=""

countryCode.description: DEPRECATED camelCase alias of country_code, kept for a deprecation window. Prefer country_code (snake_case is our canonical convention). ISO country code for the location; null for supernames like Worldwide and for locations X reports no code for.

country_code.description: ISO country code for the location; null for supernames like Worldwide and for locations X reports no code for. Canonical snake_case field (carries the same value as the deprecated camelCase countryCode).

parentid.description: WOEID of the parent location (0 for the top-level Worldwide supername).

placeType.description: DEPRECATED camelCase alias of place_type, kept for a deprecation window. Prefer place_type. The location's place-type classification.

code.description: Numeric place-type code (for example 19 for a supername, 12 for a country, 7 for a town).

name.description: Human-readable place-type name, for example "Supername", "Country", or "Town".

place_type.description: The location's place-type classification. Canonical snake_case field (carries the same value as the deprecated camelCase placeType).

code.description: Numeric place-type code (for example 19 for a supername, 12 for a country, 7 for a town).

name.description: Human-readable place-type name, for example "Supername", "Country", or "Town".

url.description: The where.yahooapis.com reference URL X returns for the location.

About.description: A profile's full About object: identity, bio, location, linked website, verification and identity-verification flags, the professional account type and categories, follower/following counts, avatar, the account-creation date, and the "About this account" transparency panel (account country, how the account was created, username-change history).

id.description: Numeric user ID as a string.

is_blue_verified.description: Whether the account carries the Verified (Blue) badge.

verified_type.description: Verification type, for example Business or Government, when applicable; null otherwise.

professional_type.description: Professional account type, for example "Creator" or "Business", when the account publishes one; null otherwise.

professional_categories.description: Professional category names the account has published (populated only for Professional/Business accounts; empty array otherwise).

items.description: A human-readable category name, for example "Software Company".

created_at.description: Account creation timestamp in Twitter date format.

is_identity_verified.description: Whether the account has completed X's identity verification. Null when the profile carries no verification_info block (an honest "not available", never a fabricated value).

verified_since.description: Timestamp the account was verified, as the raw epoch-milliseconds string X emits; null when not available.

account_based_in.description: Country the account is based in, from X's "About this account" transparency panel; null when the panel is unavailable.

created_via.description: How the account was created, from X's "About this account" transparency panel, for example "United States App Store". X names this field `source` upstream; it is surfaced here as created_via (the "connected via / created via" concept). Null when the panel is unavailable.

username_changes.description: Username-change history from X's "About this account" transparency panel; null when the panel is unavailable.

count.description: Number of times the account has changed its username.

last_changed_at.description: When the username was last changed, as the raw epoch-milliseconds string X emits; null when the account has never changed its username (count is 0).

created_country_accurate.description: Whether X considers account_based_in an accurate reflection of the account's country of origin; null when the transparency panel is unavailable.

location_accurate.description: Whether X considers the self-reported location accurate; null when the transparency panel is unavailable.

learn_more_url.description: X help-center link explaining the "About this account" transparency data; null when the panel is unavailable.

protected.description: Whether the account is locked, so only approved followers can see its posts. Null on a trimmed user object that carries no protected key, which is an honest "not available" rather than a claim the account is public.

affiliate_label.description: The affiliation badge X shows beside the display name, linking the account to a parent organization. Null when the account has no affiliation.

description.description: The parent organization's display name, for example "X".

badge_url.description: URL of the small badge image X renders next to the name.

url.description: Link to the parent organization's profile.

about_profile.description: The profile About card and the "About this account" transparency panel grouped into one object, alongside the flat fields above. Every member mirrors a flat field of the same meaning except birthdate, which appears nowhere else in the response. The object itself is always present on a resolved profile; each member is null when X did not send it.

bio.description: Profile bio text. Same value as the flat description field.

location.description: Self-reported location. Same value as the flat location field, and an empty string when the account set none.

website.description: Linked website URL. Same value as the flat url field, and an empty string when the account set none.

birthdate.description: Birthday from the About card, returned only when the account has one set and makes it visible. Null otherwise. Parts X withholds come back null individually, so a birthday shown as a day and month with no year returns year null.

year.description: Year; null when the account hides it.

visibility.description: Who the account shows the birthday to, for example Public, Followers, or Self.

account_based_in.description: Country the account is based in, from the transparency panel. Same value as the flat account_based_in field.

created_via.description: How the account was created, for example "United States App Store" or "Web". Same value as the flat created_via field.

username_changes.description: Username-change history from the transparency panel. Same value as the flat username_changes field.

count.description: Number of times the account has changed its username.

last_changed_at.description: When the username was last changed, as the raw epoch-milliseconds string X emits; null when the account has never changed it.

created_country_accurate.description: Whether X considers account_based_in an accurate reflection of where the account was created.

location_accurate.description: Whether X considers the self-reported location accurate.

learn_more_url.description: X help-center link explaining the transparency data.

identity_label.description: The identity badge X shows on business and organisation profiles. Three states, and they are not interchangeable: null means X sent no block, so we do not know; an object whose label is null means X sent an empty block, so the account has no identity label; an object with a populated label is a real badge. Null on every account sampled so far.

label.description: The badge itself. Null when X sent the block but the account carries no label.

description.description: The label text, for example the organisation name.

badge_url.description: URL of the badge image X renders beside the display name.

url_type.description: The kind of link X attached to the badge.

display_type.description: How X displays the label on the profile.

label_type.description: The label category X assigned, for example a business or government label.

PageInfo.description: Cursor-pagination fields present on every paged response.

count.description: Number of items returned in this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Null on the final page for list and affiliate endpoints; follower-graph endpoints return a non-null cursor even on the last page, so stop when the collection array is empty.

Relationship.description: The directional follow/block/mute relationship between a source and target account.

source_id.description: Numeric ID of the source account.

target_id.description: Numeric ID of the target account.

following.description: True when the source account follows the target.

followed_by.description: True when the target account follows the source.

blocking.description: True when the source blocks the target; null when not available.

blocked_by.description: True when the source is blocked by the target; null when not available.

muting.description: True when the source mutes the target; null when not available.

can_dm.description: True when the source can send a direct message to the target. Null when X does not say.

conversation_id.description: Conversation ID; pass to the DM conversation endpoint to read messages.

type.description: Conversation type, for example ONE_TO_ONE or GROUP_DM; may be null.

participants.description: Numeric user IDs of the participants.

DMMessage.description: A single Direct Message within a conversation.

id.description: Numeric message ID as a string.

time.description: Send time in epoch milliseconds as a string; may be null.

sender_id.description: Numeric ID of the sending account as a string; may be null.

Community.description: An X Community. Returned by Community Info and by Community Memberships, always with the same 24 keys, but NOT with the same fields populated: Community Info is served by a reduced X operation and returns admin, invites_policy, question, search_tags and members_facepile_ids empty, moderator_count as 0, and creator with id and name null. Community Memberships returns all of those filled. Each property below states which endpoint fills it, so a null can be read correctly rather than guessed at.

id.description: Numeric community id as a string.

name.description: The community's display name. Returned identically by both endpoints.

description.description: The community's description text. Null when the community has not written one, which was 1 of 39 communities sampled. Returned identically by both endpoints.

created_at.description: Millisecond epoch the community was created, as an integer rather than an ISO string. 0 when X did not send it. Returned identically by both endpoints.

member_count.description: Total members. Returned identically by both endpoints: it matched exactly on all 10 communities read through both on 2026-08-17, including one at 265135 members. Contrast moderator_count, which does not match.

moderator_count.description: Total moderators, but only from Community Memberships. COMMUNITY INFO RETURNS 0 HERE FOR EVERY COMMUNITY, including communities that demonstrably have moderators. On 10 communities read through both endpoints on 2026-08-17, Community Memberships returned 1 to 6 and Community Info returned 0 every time, and the Community Moderators roster independently agreed with Community Memberships on all 5 it was checked against. Read a 0 from Community Info as not reported, never as no moderators.

join_policy.description: How the community admits members, passed through from X. Observed values: Open and RestrictedJoinRequestsRequireModeratorApproval. Only those two have been seen, which is not the same as those two being the whole set, so the field is passed through as a string rather than narrowed to an enum. Returned identically by both endpoints.

invites_policy.description: Who may invite new members, passed through from X. Observed values: MemberInvitesAllowed and ModeratorInvitesAllowed. ONLY COMMUNITY MEMBERSHIPS RETURNS IT. Community Info returns null here for every community, so a null from that endpoint means the operation serving it does not carry the field, NOT that the community has no invite policy. The two cases cannot be told apart from the response alone, which is why it is stated here: on 2026-08-17 this field was non-null on all 10 communities read through Community Memberships and null on the same 10 read through Community Info minutes later. When you need the invite policy, read it from Community Memberships.

is_nsfw.description: Whether the community is flagged not-safe-for-work. Defaults to false when X does not send the field, so an absent flag reads as not flagged rather than as unknown. Returned identically by both endpoints.

question.description: The join-screen prompt applicants answer, when the community sets one. Community Info returns null here for every community, including ones that do set a question, so read it from Community Memberships. A null from Community Memberships is the real answer and means the community asks nothing.

primary_topic.description: The single topic X assigns the community. Null when the community has no topic. Community Info fills name but leaves topic_id null, so take topic_id from Community Memberships if you need the numeric id. X spells the name topic_name on the wire; it is normalised to name so a consumer reading Spaces topics and Community topics does not have to care.

topic_id.description: X's numeric topic id as a string, for example 603 for Entrepreneurship. Null on Community Info, which sends the name without the id.

name.description: The topic's display name, for example Entrepreneurship or Education. Filled by both endpoints.

search_tags.description: The community's search tags, as plain strings. Community Info returns an empty array for every community, including ones that do have tags, so read this from Community Memberships. An empty array from Community Memberships is the real answer and means the community set none.

items.description: One search tag, without a leading hash.

rules.description: The community's posted rules, in the order X returns them. Returned identically by both endpoints.

id.description: Numeric rule id as a string.

name.description: The rule's title, which is the line X shows in the community's rule list.

description.description: The longer body text under the rule's title. Null when the community left it blank, which was 87 of 174 rules sampled on 2026-08-17, so expect roughly half of them to carry only a name. It is left null rather than filled with the rule name.

banner_url.description: The banner a client should actually render: the custom banner when the community set one, otherwise X's default. Computed for you, because both banners are always present and picking the wrong one silently shows every community the same stock gradient. Returned identically by both endpoints.

custom_banner.description: The community's own banner, or null when the community never set one. Returned identically by both endpoints.

default_banner.description: X's stock banner. Present even when a custom banner exists, which is why banner_url is computed rather than left to the caller. Returned identically by both endpoints.

permalink.description: ALWAYS NULL, on both endpoints. X's community payload does not carry a permalink URL on either operation, and one is not synthesised here from the id. It was null on every community record sampled on 2026-08-17, through both endpoints. Build the link yourself: https://x.com/i/communities/ followed by the id.

admin.description: The community admin's full user profile, but only from Community Memberships. COMMUNITY INFO RETURNS NULL HERE FOR EVERY COMMUNITY: a full profile came back on all 10 communities read through Community Memberships on 2026-08-17 and null on the same 10 read through Community Info. If you need the admin and are starting from a community id, page Community Moderators, whose Admin row carries the same account.

creator.description: The community creator's full user profile, but only from Community Memberships. Community Info returns a REDUCED object here with id and name null, carrying the username and the verification flags and nothing else, so treat what Community Info gives you as a handle rather than a profile. Frequently the same account as admin, but do not assume it always is.

members_facepile_ids.description: User ids of the members X puts in the community facepile preview, ids only. Community Info returns an empty array for every community, so read this from Community Memberships. Use Community Members for the actual roster, which is the right tool whichever endpoint you started from.

items.description: A numeric user id as a string.

role.description: ALWAYS NULL, on both endpoints. It is the role of the ACCOUNT THAT MADE THE CALL, and these are pooled reads served by a rotating pool account, so any value here would describe a stranger. The key is kept rather than removed so it stays visible that X sends this field and we decline to answer it. For a real per-member role, use Community Members, whose members[].role is about that member and not about the caller.

can_join.description: ALWAYS NULL, on both endpoints, for the same caller-relative reason as role. It answers whether the CALLING account may join, and the calling account is one of ours. Use join_policy for the community's own admission rule, which is a real answer.

is_pinned.description: ALWAYS NULL, on both endpoints, for the same caller-relative reason as role. It answers whether the CALLING account pinned this community.

viewer_relationship_type.description: ALWAYS NULL, on both endpoints, for the same caller-relative reason as role. It is the viewer relationship, and the viewer is the pool account.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The uniform JSON body returned on every non-2xx response.

error.description: Machine-readable error code, for example bad_request, unauthorized, or not_found.

paid_promotion.name: paid_promotion
paid_promotion.description: Filter this page's tweets by X's Paid partnership label: only keeps tweets whose is_paid_promotion is true, exclude keeps the rest. Omit it for every tweet. It filters the page X returned and does not fetch more, so a filtered page can hold fewer tweets than asked for, or none, while next_cursor still pages on. The response carries paid_promotion_filter { mode, kept, removed }, and count reflects what is returned. Any other value is a 400. Billing is the same as without it.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated list of dotted field paths to keep in the response (one parameter, never repeated), applied to every object in the returned lists and to nested objects (for example fields=id,text,author.username; the list's own name may prefix a path, fields=tweets.id). A path prefix that lands on an array applies to each element (media.media_url_https). Pagination and envelope keys (next_cursor, cursor, has_more, count, partial, error, message, reason) are always kept. Unknown paths are ignored; up to 50 paths of up to 6 segments. Projection never changes status codes or billing, and applies to data reads only: account, feedback, session status, monitor (other than deliveries), webhook and stream-compat reads return their bodies unchanged.

compact.name: compact
compact.description: Set to 1 (or true) to apply the built-in compact preset: ids, url, text, created_at, lang, the engagement counts, the is_retweet/is_reply/is_quote flags, conversation ids, the author's id/username/name/followers_count/verification, and the quoted or retweeted tweet's id/url/author username. The preset trims what it recognises and leaves alone what it would empty, so it never turns a body into {}. Combine with fields to add paths on top of the preset. Typically cuts a tweet page by 70 to 90 percent for LLM tool callers.

bearerAuth.description: Pass your API key as a bearer token on every request: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Your API account: credit balance, usage totals, payment history, and product feedback filed from the tool you are using. Served from the API root (https://api.twitterapis.com/account/* and /feedback), not under /twitter, because billing owns their authentication. Free.

tags.name: Account Session
tags.description: Bring your own X session cookies (recommended), or mint a session from a username and password, so write actions and private-data reads act as your account. Free.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Full-text and structured search across tweets and users. Filter by query operators, author, date, language, and engagement.

tags.name: Tweet Details
tags.description: Resolve a single tweet into its full object: replies, retweeters, and the complete conversation thread.

tags.name: User Reads
tags.description: Read a profile, its timeline, media, mentions, affiliates, and follow relationships by username or numeric ID.

tags.name: Direct Messages
tags.description: Read your account's DM inbox and the message history of a single conversation, and send new messages, all acting as the account behind your registered session.

tags.name: Follower Graph
tags.description: Page through followers and following lists, including the verified-only and v2 cursor-paginated variants.

tags.name: List Data
tags.description: Read the members of any public Twitter/X List.

tags.name: Trends
tags.description: Read what is trending on Twitter/X right now, worldwide, for a single country, for one X Explore tab or for the trends X labels Business and finance, plus the full set of locations trends are available for.

tags.name: Spaces
tags.description: Read an X Space by id: title, host, speakers, topics, timing and audience counts, for a Space that is scheduled, running or already ended.

tags.name: Communities
tags.description: Read an X Community: its metadata and rules, its member and moderator rosters, its own post timeline including the pinned post, and the inverse relation, every community a given account belongs to. These are pooled reads served by our account pool, so the four fields that describe the CALLER's own relationship to a community (role, can_join, is_pinned, viewer_relationship_type) always come back null.

tags.name: Write Actions
tags.description: Act on behalf of an authenticated account: post, delete, like, retweet, bookmark and follow, each with its undo, plus the compose surface (private drafts and scheduled posts). MOST of these bill at $0.0008 per call, the same as a standard read, but not all: tweet/create, draft/create, draft/edit, draft/list, scheduled/create and scheduled/list are $0.0016. Read the price on the endpoint, never off this line.

tags.name: Articles
tags.description: Create, edit, publish, and read X's long-form Articles (X's internal name: Notes). Publishing posts a real announcement tweet; reading a published article is a public call that needs no session.

tags.name: Grok
tags.description: Ask X's own in-app Grok a question and get the answer back with the pages it cited. Grok reads X in real time, so it answers about posts and accounts a general model has never seen. Runs as your account, returns one buffered JSON document rather than a stream, and stores nothing: you pass prior turns back yourself.

tags.name: Monitoring
tags.description: Watch an X account for new posts and get them pushed to your own webhook, HMAC-signed, retried for 21 minutes on failure. Polls on a shared interval and never spends your read credits: monitor and webhook management are free account administration, not metered reads.
